arxiv-2103-13510.title: A scalable hierarchical lasso for gene-environment interactions
arxiv-2103-13510.creator: Natalia Zemlianskaia
arxiv-2103-13510.description: Abstract We describe a regularized regression model for the selection of gene-environment (G × \times E) interactions. The model focuses on a single environmental exposure and induces a main-effect-before-interaction hierarchical structure. We propose an efficient fitting algorithm and screening rules that can discard large numbers of irrelevant predictors with high accuracy.

arxiv-2311-13944.title: Investigating microstructure-property relationships of nonwovens by model-based virtual materials testing
arxiv-2311-13944.creator: Matthias Weber, Andreas Grießer, Dennis Mosbach, Erik Glatt, Andreas Wiegmann, Volker Schmidt
arxiv-2311-13944.description: Abstract Quantifying the relationship between geometric descriptors of microstructure and effective properties like permeability is essential for understanding and improving the behavior of porous materials. In this paper, we employ a previously developed stochastic model to investigate microstructure-property relationships of nonwovens.

arxiv-2408-13048.title: Asset pricing under model uncertainty with finite time and states
arxiv-2408-13048.creator: Shuzhen Yang, Wenqing Zhang
arxiv-2408-13048.description: Abstract In this study, we consider the asset pricing under model uncertainty with finite time and states structure. For the single-period securities model, we give a novel definition of arbitrage under a family of probability, and explore its relationship with risk neutral probability measure.

arxiv-2408-16362.title: Oscillatory dependence of tunneling magnetoresistance on barrier thickness in magnetic tunnel junctions
arxiv-2408-16362.creator: B. C. Lee
arxiv-2408-16362.description: Abstract The dependence of tunneling conductance and tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR) on barrier thickness in magnetic tunnel junctions is theoretically investigated. The complex band structure of the insulator is taken into account, and an analytical formula for tunneling conductance and TMR is derived. Numerical calculations using a tight-binding model validate the analytical formula.

arxiv-2601-13274.title: Structure and Memory Control Self-Diffusion in Active Matter
arxiv-2601-13274.creator: Akinlade Akintunde, Stewart A. Mallory
arxiv-2601-13274.description: Abstract Despite extensive progress in characterizing the emergent behavior of active matter, the microscopic origins of self-diffusion in interacting active systems remain poorly understood. Here, we develop a framework that quantitatively links self-diffusion to collisional forces and their temporal correlations in active fluids.

pmc-11491960.title: The Effect of FTY720 on Sphingolipid Imbalance and Cognitive Decline in Aged EFAD Mice
pmc-11491960.creator: Qian Luo, Simone M. Crivelli, Shenghua Zong, Caterina Giovagnoni, Daan van Kruining, Marina Mané-Damas, Sandra den Hoedt, Dusan Berkes, Helga E. De Vries, Monique T. Mulder, Jochen Walter, Etienne Waelkens, Rita Derua, Johannes V. Swinnen, Jonas Dehairs, Mario Losen, Pilar Martinez-Martinez
pmc-11491960.description: Background:During Alzheimer’s disease (AD) progression, there is a decline in the bioactive sphingolipid sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P). Previous research showed that FTY720, an S1P mimetic, prevented cognitive decline and reduced ceramide levels in transgenic mice with familial AD carrying the human APOE4 gene (E4FAD) at 6–7 months of age.

pmc-11533314.title: Exosomes derived from platelet-rich plasma present a novel potential in repairing knee articular cartilage defect combined with cyclic peptide-modified β-TCP scaffold
pmc-11533314.creator: Xuchang Liu, Rudong Chen, Guanzheng Cui, Rongjie Feng, Kechun Liu
pmc-11533314.description: BackgroundThe aim of this study was to investigate the therapeutic effects and mechanisms of PRP-exos combined with cyclic peptide-modified β-TCP scaffold in the treatment of rabbit knee cartilage defect.MethodsPRP-exos were extracted and characterized by TEM, NTA and WB. The therapeutic effects were evaluated by ICRS score, HE staining, Immunohistochemistry, qRT-PCR and ELISA.

pmc-12126193.title: Relationship between Color-Coded Anatomical M-Mode, Strain Imaging, and Tissue Doppler Imaging in Assessing Myocardial Asynchrony in Normal Subjects
pmc-12126193.creator: Mohammad Amin Masoumi, Masoumeh Lotfi Tokaldani, Saman Sarhangzadeh, Parto Siavosh, Hakimeh Sadeghian
pmc-12126193.description: Background:This study aimed to compare the time-to-peak systolic contraction time (Tc) by color-coded anatomical M-mode (AMM), the time-to-peak systolic strain (Tst) by strain rate imaging (SRI), and the time-to-peak systolic velocity (Ts) by tissue Doppler imaging (TDI) in the left (LV) and right (RV) ventricular segments of normal subjects.

pmc-12575892.title: Multimodal CT radiomics predicts PD-1 inhibitor efficacy in advanced gastric cancer: a two-center validation study
pmc-12575892.creator: Zhipeng Wang, Yinchao Ma, Jiahe Tan, Ming Li, Chenyang Qiu, Kun Han, Shuzhen Wu, Haiyan Wang
pmc-12575892.description: ObjectivesIn this study, we developed a multi-modal CT-based machine learning model to predict the response of gastric cancer (GC) patients to first-line chemotherapy combined with PD-1 inhibitors and performed external validation and multi-model comparisons.Materials and methodsWe retrospectively analyzed the clinical data of 348 patients with GC who underwent immunotherapy.

pmc-13187694.title: Impact of Frailty Risk on Adverse Outcomes after Open Heart Valve Surgery in Older Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13187694.creator: Issei Kameda, Akio Shimizu, Kenta Ushida, Miho Shimizu, Kohei Ochiai, Yuki Kato, Ryo Momosaki
pmc-13187694.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Objectives:This study aimed to investigate the impact of preoperative frailty risk, assessed using the Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS), on hospitalization-associated disability (HAD) and in-hospital complications in patients aged 65 years or older who underwent open heart valve surgery.Methods:This retrospective cohort study included patients in the JMDC database aged 65 years or older with valvular heart disease who underwent open heart valve surgery between April 2017 and December 2022.

pmc-13200535.title: Comparative review of artificial intelligence for transcriptomic biomarker discovery in coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19)
pmc-13200535.creator: Li Ying Khoo, Sarinder Kaur Dhillon
pmc-13200535.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic has highlighted the significance of reliable molecular biomarkers in clinical use. Despite the popularity of traditional statistical approaches, the high dimensionality of transcriptomic data presents challenges for these conventional methods. While artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms have emerged as highly advantageous for handling these complex datasets, there is a lack of evaluation of these approaches in COVID-19 transcriptomic studies.

pmc-13317338.creator: Joan Kleine, Dorothea Kohnen, Alessandro Campione, Reinhard Busse
